question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in sandbox-to-ACP bridge/placement contract, and which security boundary should own host-side ACP spawn, steer, and cancel requests from sandboxed sessions?
rationale: The requested behavior intentionally crosses a sandbox-to-host execution boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent privilege, config, audit, and failure model.

options.title: Define A Narrow ACP Bridge Contract
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in bridge/proxy or placement contract with requester allowlists, logged spawn/steer/cancel verbs, rate limits, and fail-closed defaults before allowing sandboxed ACP spawns.

options.title: Fold Into Execution Backends
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 the design home and require the execution-backend contract to cover sandboxed ACP before this issue is implemented.

options.title: Keep ACP Host-Only
options.body: Keep sandboxed requesters blocked and document container-local harness installation or native subagents as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Define A Narrow ACP Bridge Contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit opt-in bridge/proxy or placement contract with requester allowlists, logged spawn/steer/cancel verbs, rate limits, and fail-closed defaults before allowing sandboxed ACP spawns.
